To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we propose a model for describing the behavior polarization observables for the deuteron scattering from nuclei at intermediate energies, based on the multiple diffractive scattering theory and α-cluster model.

the multiple diffraction approach with the α-cluster model and dispersion of target nuclei provides an adequate description of the elastic deuteron-nucleus scattering in the intermediate energy range.

the model based on the theory of multiple diffraction scattering from a target with dispersion of its internal structure is in a good agreement with experimental data for the elastic deutereon scattering from 12 C and 16 O nuclei at intermediate energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the deuteron scattering from nuclei at intermediate energies.
the study of the polarization phenomena in the elastic deuteron-deuteron scattering at intermediate energies.
the study of polarization phenomena in the elastic scattering of deuterons from the nuclei 12C and16O at intermediate energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the multiple-scattering model with dispersion of nuclear matter density is able to describe reasonably well the elastic deuteron-nucleus scattering data for incident energies from 200 MeV to 800 MeV.
the α-cluster model of 16C and dispersion of target nuclei are important ingredients for the description of elastic deuteron scattering on 16C and, probably, on 12C nuclei at intermediate energies.
the model based on the α-cluster model and the dispersion theory for target nuclei can be used to describe the elastic deuteron-scattering from 12C, 16O and 16C nuclei at intermediate energies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the multiple diffraction model with dispersion can describe the experimental data for the elastic scattering from 12,16C and 12,16O nuclei at 400 and 720 MeV incident energies.

the α-cluster model for the target nuclei and the multiple diffraction approach for the deuteron scattering are able to explain the main features of polarization observables in deuteron scattering from nuclei at energies of 400 MeV and higher.

a multiple diffraction scattering model with the α-cluster model for the description of deuteron-nucleus interaction at intermediate energies is a promising approach for the description of elastic scattering observables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the polarization observables for the intermediate energy deuteron scattering from nuclei can be described within a model based on the α-cluster picture for nuclei.
the α-cluster model is a good approximation to describe the intermediate energy elastic scattering of the deuteron from 16C nucleus.
the polarization phenomena are caused by the dispersion of the α-cluster structure of 16C and the multiple diffraction mechanism of the deuteron scattering from the α-cluster.
